title: Guardrails
description: The abort conditions, decided before anything goes live (R10). Built by Lane A's sentence-with-blanks UI, stored immutably on the rollout, evaluated by Lane B's cron. Every rule reads as one plain sentence; `sentence` is what the merchant saw when they agreed to it and must be persisted verbatim.

auto_rollback.description: false = alert only; the evaluator pauses and emails instead of reverting. Open pilot question in the PRD, so it is a first-class field.

id.description: Stable within the rollout; referenced by breach events.

metric.description: profit rules are only evaluated when every affected variant has COGS; otherwise the rule is skipped and the skip is journalled, never silently treated as passing.

comparison.description: below_expected_pct compares to the expected band (model or bracket). below_absolute compares to a fixed daily floor.

threshold_pct.description: Required for below_expected_pct. 30 means 'more than 30% below expected', i.e. actual < expected * 0.70.

absolute_floor.description: Required for below_absolute: units/day, or cents/day for revenue and profit metrics.

consecutive_days.description: Days in a row the condition must hold before the action fires. 1 is allowed but noisy for small stores.

scope.description: rollout = the selection in aggregate (quieter, the default). product = any single affected variant trips it.

action.description: rollback_all restores every price this rollout changed, from the baselines captured at creation. pause stops advancing and emails.

min_expected_units.description: Low-volume floor. When expected units for the day are below this, the day cannot register a breach on its own — random zeros are not evidence. Lane B defaults it to 3.0 when omitted (see lib/engine/guardrails.ts).

sentence.description: Exactly what the merchant read, e.g. 'If daily units fall more than 30% below expected for 2 days in a row, revert everything automatically.'
